key_insight: Price-based decentralized scheduling of EVs and heat pumps can synchronize flexible demand so strongly that feeder peaks exceed those from uncoordinated operation.
engineering_relevance: For low-voltage distribution planning and tariff design, the study shows that local cost minimization can worsen transformer loading and voltage quality unless explicit network constraints are included.
method: Simulated a rural low-voltage feeder with 97 buses and a 250 kVA transformer.
Ran 160 simulations across seven scenarios, four seasons, and 0–90% penetration of EVs, heat pumps, and PV.
Compared uncoordinated operation, decentralized price minimization, fixed schedules, and central transformer-capped scheduling.
evidence_signal: At 30% penetration of EVs and heat pumps, decentralized price minimization drove the transformer to 253% of rated capacity, with peaks up to 478% at 90% EV penetration, and the first undervoltage violations appeared at the feeder end.
watch_item: Results depend on feeder topology, seasonal conditions, and device mix, so the conclusions should not be generalized without local grid validation.
paper_title: Price-Optimized EV and Heat-Pump Scheduling Can Exceed Uncoordinated Feeder Peaks
